page.title: Legal Deadline Calculator
page.description: Choose the date you were served with or notified of a judgment or decision (or the date it was pronounced) and the procedure (civil appeal 2 weeks, criminal appeal 7 days, immediate appeal, final appeal, objection, etc.) to calculate the deadline, taking public holidays and substitute holidays into account.
page.lead: Calculates when a deadline set by law, such as for an appeal, a final appeal or an objection, ends. The first day is not counted, and if the last day falls on a weekend or public holiday, the deadline moves to the next day.
page.notice: This date is for reference only and follows the general calculation method in the law. If you have the date of service wrong or a special rule applies, the deadline will be different. Once a deadline passes, it is hard to challenge the decision again, so if the deadline is close, talk to a lawyer right away.

ui.baseHint: The date you were served with or notified of the judgment or decision
ui.zeroHour: Service took effect at 00:00 that day (for example, an e-litigation document deemed served because it was not opened for 1 week) — the first day is counted
ui.arrive: Documents must reach the court by the deadline (for mail, what counts is the date it arrives, not the date it was sent).
ui.firstZero: First day (counted from that day because service took effect at 00:00)
ui.firstNext: First day (counting starts the next day)
ui.fixedNote: A peremptory period is a period that even the court cannot extend. As a rule, missing it by even one day means losing the chance to challenge the decision, so file with time to spare.
ui.outside: Public holidays are only included from {from} to {to}. For dates outside this range only Saturdays and Sundays were taken into account, so please check public holidays on a calendar as well.
ui.method: How it is calculated: the first day of the period is not counted; counting starts the next day (Civil Act, Article 157; Criminal Procedure Act, Article 66(1)). If the last day is a Saturday, Sunday or public holiday, the period is extended to the following day (Civil Act, Article 161; Criminal Procedure Act, Article 66(3)). Public holidays are the public holidays and substitute holidays under the Regulations on Holidays of Government Offices.

civil-appeal.label: Appeal
civil-appeal.from: The date you were served with the written judgment
civil-appeal.basis: Civil Procedure Act, Article 396(1) (applied to administrative litigation under Administrative Litigation Act, Article 8)

civil-final.label: Final appeal to the Supreme Court
civil-final.from: The date you were served with the appellate judgment

civil-appeal-brief.label: Filing the statement of grounds for appeal
civil-appeal-brief.from: The date you received notice that the appeal record was received
civil-appeal-brief.note: The court may extend it once, by up to 1 month (paragraph 2 of the same Article).

civil-final-brief.label: Filing the statement of grounds for final appeal
civil-final-brief.from: The date you received notice that the final appeal record was received

civil-immediate.label: Immediate appeal
civil-immediate.from: The date you were notified of the decision or order

civil-special.label: Special appeal
civil-special.from: The date you were notified of the decision or order

civil-reconcile.label: Objection to a decision recommending settlement
civil-reconcile.from: The date you were served with the original copy of the decision

civil-small.label: Objection to a decision recommending performance
civil-small.from: The date you were served with a certified copy of the decision recommending performance

civil-payment.label: Objection to a payment order
civil-payment.from: The date you were served with the payment order

civil-mediation.label: Objection to a decision in lieu of conciliation
civil-mediation.from: The date you were served with the original copy of the decision record

civil-answer.label: Filing an answer
civil-answer.from: The date you were served with a copy of the complaint
civil-answer.note: This is not a peremptory period, but if you miss it, the court may rule for the plaintiff without a hearing.

exec-immediate.label: Immediate appeal against a decision of the execution court
exec-immediate.from: The date you were notified of the decision

exec-brief.label: Filing the statement of grounds for immediate appeal
exec-brief.from: The date you filed the petition of appeal

family-appeal.label: Appeal in a family litigation case
family-appeal.from: The date you were served with the original copy of the judgment

family-immediate.label: Immediate appeal against a ruling in a family non-litigation case
family-immediate.from: The date you were notified of the ruling
family-immediate.note: The starting date may differ depending on who appeals (Family Litigation Rules).

crim-appeal.label: Criminal appeal
crim-appeal.from: The date the judgment was pronounced

crim-final.label: Criminal final appeal to the Supreme Court
crim-final.from: The date the appellate judgment was pronounced

crim-appeal-brief.label: Filing the statement of grounds for a criminal appeal
crim-appeal-brief.from: The date you received notice that the case record was received

crim-final-brief.label: Filing the statement of grounds for a criminal final appeal
crim-final-brief.from: The date you received notice that the case record was received

crim-summary.label: Request for a formal trial against a summary order
crim-summary.from: The date you were notified of (served with) the summary order

crim-immediate.label: Criminal immediate appeal
crim-immediate.from: The date the decision was announced

admin-trial.label: Filing an administrative appeal
admin-trial.from: The date you learned of the administrative disposition
admin-trial.note: You cannot file once 180 days have passed since the disposition was made (paragraph 3 of the same Article).

admin-suit.label: Filing a revocation lawsuit
admin-suit.from: The date you learned of the disposition (if you went through an administrative appeal, the date you were served with the original copy of the ruling)
admin-suit.note: You cannot file once 1 year has passed since the disposition (or the ruling) was made (paragraph 2 of the same Article).

const-complaint.label: Filing a constitutional complaint
const-complaint.from: The date you learned of the cause of the infringement of your basic rights
const-complaint.note: You must also file within 1 year from the date the cause arose.
